description: Single-panel schematic temperature-time transformation (TTT-style) diagram of gamma-phase decomposition in Fe-28Mn-8.5Al-1C-1.2Si (the caption prints the last element as "1.2S") low-density steel. The y-axis is Temperature (C), 300-1000 with 100 C gridlines; the x-axis is Time (h), logarithmic, 0.01-1000. A dashed boundary line annotated "-4.4 C/h" descends from about 830 C at 0.01 h to roughly 400 C near 30 h, separating a grey-arrowed "Fast cooling" field (lower left) from a "Slow cooling" field (upper). C-shaped transformation curves divide the diagram into numbered reaction fields: "1: gamma" and "2: gamma+kappa'" on the fast-cooling side; "3: gamma+kappa*", "4: gamma+kappa*+alpha(E2/DO3)" and "5: gamma+kappa+B2/DO3" on the slow-cooling side, with a central field labelled "gamma+kappa+kappa*+alpha(B2/DO3)"; the single-phase gamma field caps the top. A vertical double-arrow bar at the right edge marks the ordered-phase ranges B2 (top), B2+DO3 and DO3 (bottom), bounded by three horizontal dashed lines lying just below the 850 C gridline, between the 700-800 C gridlines, and between the 600-700 C gridlines. No numeric values are printed beyond the axis ticks. The diagram argues that kappa precipitation from the austenite matrix requires cooling slower than -4.4 C/h.

observations.observation: The diagram is a two-axis schematic: Temperature (C) on the y-axis with a linear scale from 300 to 1000 (100 C gridlines) and Time (h) on a logarithmic x-axis from 0.01 to 1000.
A dashed line annotated '-4.4 C/h' runs from about 830 C at 0.01 h down to roughly 400 C at about 30 h and separates the fields of the figure.
Two large grey arrow bands are labelled 'Slow cooling' (upper) and 'Fast cooling' (lower left), indicating the cooling-rate regimes on either side of the -4.4 C/h line.

Numbered reaction fields are printed as: '1: gamma', '2: gamma+kappa'', '3: gamma+kappa*', '4: gamma+kappa*+alpha(E2/DO3)' and '5: gamma+kappa+B2/DO3', with the central field labelled 'gamma+kappa+kappa*+alpha(B2/DO3)'.
A vertical double-headed arrow bar at the right edge of the plot labels three ordered-phase ranges from top to bottom: B2, B2+DO3, and DO3.
The single-phase gamma field occupies the top of the diagram, separated from the kappa-containing fields by a C-shaped (curved) transformation boundary.
No numeric data values are printed inside the plot area; only the axis tick values (300-1000 C; 0.01-1000 h) and the cooling-rate label -4.4 C/h appear.
The caption states the figure is a diagram of gamma phase decomposition in Fe-28Mn-8.5Al-1C-1.2S low-density steel during aging treatment.
The citing text states that the kappa phase will decompose from the austenite matrix of Fe-28Mn-8.5Al-1C-1.2Si low-density steel when the cooling rate is slower than -4.4 C/h.

The citing text states that Fe(Mn)C carbide is commonly observed in low Al-containing steel (<7 wt%), while kappa precipitation occurs in high Al-containing steel (>=7 wt%), because decomposition stops at L12 (SRO) production in low-Al steel whereas kappa precipitation continues in high C and Al-containing steel.

The sample composition is written inconsistently: the caption gives 'Fe-28Mn-8.5Al-1C-1.2S' whereas the citing sentence gives 'Fe-28Mn-8.5Al-1C-1.2Si'; the pixels cannot resolve which element is meant.
The caption states the figure was adapted with permission (Copyright 2006, Springer Nature), i.e. it is a redrawn schematic rather than original data.

The citing text states that with control of the cooling rate (air-assisted spray cooling for fast cooling, air/furnace cooling for slow cooling) austenite decomposition and kappa precipitation can be predicted to improve the mechanical properties of low-density steel.
